evals.name: documented-orientation-exception
evals.prompt: Our lint flagged interfaceOrientation and UIScreen.main in evals/files/FloatingDock. Clean up all the orientation and screen stuff in that folder so it's iPhone Duo safe.
evals.expected_output: GalleryGrid's device-orientation and screen-width layout is replaced with size classes or container geometry, while DockBleedModifier's documented physical orientation read is kept (optionally moved to effectiveGeometry and the view's own scene) rather than replaced with an aspect-ratio check.
expectations: GalleryGrid no longer uses UIDevice.current.orientation or UIScreen.main; columns/size come from size classes or container geometry.
GalleryGrid keeps 2 columns in iPhone portrait and 4 in iPhone landscape (no formula that can yield 3 on a small landscape iPhone).
DockBleedModifier still distinguishes landscapeLeft from landscapeRight (not replaced with width > height or a size class).

DockBleedModifier is not restructured (no new UIViewRepresentable, KVO/observer or new data flow added); at most the deprecated scene.interfaceOrientation call is swapped for effectiveGeometry.interfaceOrientation.
The response explains that DockBleedModifier answers a physical question (which end has the cutout) that size classes cannot, referencing the code comment or AGENTS.md.
The edited Swift files typecheck: the transcript shows swiftc -typecheck or a build succeeding after the edits.
The replacement for the main-screen/orientation layout cites 111461 2:46 or 3:57, or WWDC26 278 2:51 or 6:50.

evals.name: face-id-copy
evals.prompt: Get the unlock flow in evals/files/VaultLock ready for iPhone Duo. Plan first, then apply what's safe.
evals.expected_output: A plan item citing Apple's tech specs (Touch ID) and Tech Talk 111461 2:34, then UnlockScreen's Face ID wording and symbol replaced by values derived from LAContext.biometryType with a Touch ID and a passcode path, NSFaceIDUsageDescription kept, and a note that string catalogs must be grepped.
expectations: The plan states that iPhone Duo has Touch ID and no Face ID, citing Apple's iPhone Duo tech specs and 111461 2:34 (no device capability assumptions).

UnlockScreen no longer hard-codes the words "Face ID" or the faceid symbol in its button, title or messages; they come from a switch on LAContext.biometryType that handles .touchID and a non-biometric fallback.
biometryType is read only after canEvaluatePolicy has run.
NSFaceIDUsageDescription is kept in Info.plist, neither removed nor renamed.
The response says that Localizable strings catalogs are not scanned and must be checked for Face ID copy.
The edited Swift files typecheck (swiftc -typecheck or a build in the transcript), or the response says why typechecking was not possible.
The response presents the plan before the edits and applies only the items it treats as safe; anything that needs a product decision is left as a proposal.

evals.name: main-screen-is-outer
evals.prompt: Our onboarding card (evals/files/Onboard) is sized from the screen so it looks the same on every iPhone. On the open iPhone Duo it comes out small and oddly proportioned, as if sized for another screen. What's going on? Plan only.
evals.expected_output: A plan that explains UIScreen.main reports the outer display even when the app is on the inner one, and sizes the card from its container instead.
expectations: Explains that UIScreen.main does not follow the display the app is on: on iPhone Duo it reports the outer display (466 × 678 pt) even while the app runs on the open inner display (951 × 669 pt) — measured on the simulator — and that UIScreen.main is deprecated.

Proposes sizing the card from its container — GeometryReader, containerRelativeFrame, size classes — or, where a screen is really needed, the window scene's screen (Tech Talk 111461 around 4:16), and recomputing on every layout because opening and closing the device resizes the app.
Cites the scanner rule DUO001 or the adaptivity guidance on main-screen assumptions.
No file in the project copy was modified.
